This idea became Cauldron-FlowGuard AI, a predictive monitoring and optimization platform for transparent, reliable operations.

Cauldron-FlowGuard AI continuously monitors cauldron levels, ticket reports, and courier activities to verify that the reported potion volumes match actual drained amounts. When the system detects unusual differences, it flags those discrepancies for review and ranks them by severity. Beyond detection, it also calculates optimized courier routes and schedules, ensuring that no cauldron overflows and that resources are used efficiently. record.problem_and_user: Security teams for whom reviewing hours of multi-camera footage manually is impractical after an incident.

devpost_first_sections: Security systems generate thousands of hours of footage - but when incidents happen, someone still has to manually scrub through timelines to find what matters. That bottleneck inspired us. We asked: What if surveillance footage could be searched like Google and queried like ChatGPT? If each camera records ( h ) hours per day and there are ( n ) cameras, total daily footage becomes: $$ F = n \times h $$ As ( n ) grows, manual review becomes impossible. With modern vision-language models and serverless GPUs becoming accessible, we saw an opportunity to transform raw video into structured, searchable intelligence — in minutes, not hours.

Vigilant AI turns raw CCTV footage into actionable intelligence. Upload a video and our system: Detects people and activities frame-by-frame Scores threat severity (Stage A → C ) Generates a structured incident report Embeds every clip as a semantic vector Makes the entire video searchable in plain English Users can ask: “Show me fights.” “When was the entrance crowded?” “Have we seen this behavior before?” And get instant answers — without watching a single frame.

devpost_first_sections: In an emergency, knowing what changed starts with knowing what is normal. For someone living with Parkinson's, tremors and movement difficulties can make that distinction harder. A clinician seeing a patient for the first time may have no record of their usual motor function, leaving a critical gap when evaluating a possible stroke. We built TapChart to make that context accessible.

TapChart connects routine motor tracking with accessible clinical context. Patients complete a short, camera-based finger-tapping test to record their motor performance over time. An NFC-linked patient profile gives doctors, EMTs, and other healthcare professionals a quick route to that information. When a patient presents with concerning symptoms, their care team can compare recent measurements with their history by tapping their tag. TapChart provides context for clinical assessment. It does not diagnose or rule out a stroke.

For the 25 million Americans who speak limited English, the label on the bottle is not even readable. The doctor did everything right, and the patient still goes home and guesses. Pharma spends billions getting a drug prescribed and loses the patient in week one. Nobody owns week one. We wanted to give every patient the thing wealthy patients already have: someone to call who knows their chart and speaks their language.

glance.what: Blink-based Morse code speech tool that tracks eye movements.
glance.why: Gives free, instant communication to people who cannot speak.

record.what_it_is: A webcam application that tracks eye blinks, treating short blinks as Morse dots and long ones as dashes, decodes them live into text and optionally speaks the text with ElevenLabs. It runs from a CLI or a Flask browser dashboard.
record.problem_and_user: People with ALS, paralysis or stroke who cannot speak or type; the page says dedicated AAC devices cost thousands of dollars.
record.one_line_pitch: Webcam blink detector that turns short and long blinks into Morse code, converts it to text and speaks it aloud with text-to-speech.
record.target_user: people with severe motor or speech impairments
record.problem_statement: People who cannot speak or use their hands need low-cost, easy-setup communication.
record.devpost_tagline: EyeCode lets your blinks do the talking. AI reads your eye movements, converts Morse code to speech, and gives instant, free communication for those who can't speak.
devpost_first_sections: Millions of people worldwide suffer from conditions like ALS, severe paralysis, strokes, and other motor disabilities, leaving them unable to speak or type. Traditional assistive communication devices can cost $7,000-$15,000, putting them out of reach for most. We were inspired to create a solution that removes these barriers and makes communication accessible to everyone. The idea struck when we realized that almost everyone already has a tool powerful enough to detect eye movements: a standard webcam. devpost_first_sections: HP's brief asked for a co-pilot for the Metal Jet S100, an industrial binder-jetting printer that sinters metal parts over hours of layered powder spreading. Components age, climates differ, sensors lie. The deliverable was a physics model, a simulator that advances time and persists state, and a grounded language interface that never invents a number.

A coupled discrete-time system over six components across three subsystems. One tick is one simulated week. Each tick, Engine.step(prev, drivers, env, dt) builds an immutable CouplingContext from the t-1 snapshot, then steps every component from the same frozen view ( sim/src/copilot_sim/engine/engine.py ). Update order cannot perturb the result. Per-tick stochasticity flows through derive_component_rng(scenario_seed, tick, component_id) keyed by a blake2b digest, so the historian is byte-identical across machines. Two state objects come out: PrinterState (true) and ObservedPrinterState (sensor-side). The maintenance agent and chat layer only read the observed one.

glance.what: Optimizes warehouse space coverage at the lowest possible cost.
glance.why: Cuts warehouse space costs through better storage coverage planning.

record.what_it_is: A Python heuristic optimizer that fills a warehouse floor with racking bays, respecting columns, uneven ceilings and walls, scored on cost versus capacity. Parallel workers pack from different corners within a 30-second limit; a Streamlit viewer lets users inspect and tweak layouts.
record.problem_and_user: Warehouse planners laying out storage bays in irregular spaces for maximum capacity at lowest cost (Mecalux challenge).
record.one_line_pitch: Python warehouse layout optimizer packing storage bays around columns and uneven ceilings using Shapely geometry and parallel exploration.
record.problem_statement: Maximizing storage capacity at minimum cost under physical constraints is a hard puzzle.
record.devpost_tagline: This project's aim is to optimize the coverage of warehouse space in the most cost-efficient possible.
devpost_first_sections: When we first saw the challenge proposed by Mecalux, we thought that it was very interesting and that it had a great similarity to a problem we did in a Programming Subject at university. Because of that, we believed it was a great way to apply our knowledge built in class to a more complex real-life problem. Beyond a classic 2D Bin Packing problem, we saw a geometric and economic puzzle where the physical rules (uneven ceilings, columns, asymmetrical walls) clash with a deceptively complex non-linear objective function. We realized that optimizing space ( Area ) and cost ( Price/Load ) sometimes pull in opposite directions, so we wanted to create an algorithm that didn't just brute-force th

We have designed a complex algorithm that uses a greedy and an aggressive automatized heuristic to minimize the objective function given by the company. In detail, we have focused on acquiring the most storage capacity, with the least cost possible. Baymaxxing ingests the warehouse topology (perimeter, obstacles, and ceiling) alongside the bay catalog to output this optimized configuration.

Research shows that 50 to 70 percent of people with autism experience hypersensitivity to everyday sounds. This inspired us to create a wearable device to help individuals with heightened sensory sensitivities manage noise pollution. Our goal is to provide a dynamic solution that adapts to changing sound environments, offering a more comfortable and controlled auditory experience.

SoundShield is a wearable device that adapts to noisy environments by automatically adjusting calming background audio and applying noise reduction. It helps individuals with sensory sensitivities block out overwhelming sounds while keeping them connected to their surroundings. The device also alerts users if someone is behind them, enhancing both awareness and comfort. It filters out unwanted noise using real-time audio processing and only plays calming music if the noise level becomes too high. glance.why: Helps recover lost items with AI and data insights.

record.what_it_is: An AI lost-and-found web app: users report or search for items, YOLO detects objects in uploaded photos and ResNet embeddings score visual similarity between lost and found items. Images sit in Azure Blob Storage, metadata in MongoDB, with Google Maps directions to the item.
record.problem_and_user: People who lose valuables; manual text descriptions and memory make matching lost and found items slow and frustrating.
record.one_line_pitch: Lost-and-found app that matches reported items to found-item images using YOLOv8 detection and ResNet similarity, then gives map directions to the item.
record.target_user: people who lost belongings; venues running lost and found
record.problem_statement: Traditional lost-and-found relies on manual descriptions and memory, making matching slow and imprecise.
record.devpost_tagline: Ever lost something precious and wished you had a digital detective on your side? Meet 404 Lost&Found – your AI-powered personal item finder and data visualization tool
devpost_first_sections: Lost and found systems have remained largely unchanged for decades, relying on manual descriptions and human memory to match items. We've all experienced the frustration of losing something valuable and the inefficiency of traditional lost and found processes. With the advancement of AI and computer vision technology, we saw an opportunity to revolutionize how people reconnect with their lost belongings using precise visual matching.

Lost and Found is a program designed to help users report and locate lost items efficiently. Using advanced video recognition technology, it identifies close matches and provides navigation assistance to guide users to their lost belongings.

glance.what: Real-time sentiment dashboard for T-Mobile product managers.
glance.why: Drives customer satisfaction through live sentiment and performance tracking.

record.what_it_is: A customer-intelligence dashboard for T-Mobile product managers. It scrapes Reddit, news and outage trackers, scores sentiment into a Customer Happiness Index by product area, maps hotspots and outages, and uses Gemini to write prioritized opportunities, PRDs and user stories.
record.problem_and_user: T-Mobile product managers who cannot tell where customers are hurting amid scattered feedback.
record.one_line_pitch: Dashboard for T-Mobile product managers that aggregates customer complaints and outage signals, maps hotspots, and uses Gemini to suggest prioritized opportunities.
record.problem_statement: Customer feedback is scattered across social media, outage trackers and forums, so PMs cannot see where customers are hurting.
record.devpost_tagline: Unified dashboard for T-Mobile PMs to track real-time customer sentiment, performance, and operational data, driving smarter, data-driven decisions and improved customer satisfaction.
devpost_first_sections: About the project We set out to give PMs the power to see, understand, and act. T‑Insight stitches together fragmented signals into a single intelligence layer: what’s happening, where it’s happening, how bad it is, and what to do next. We built a scalable ingestion pipeline, a thoughtful UI that emphasizes clarity, and an AI layer that transforms insights into prioritized opportunities. Along the way, we solved SSR pitfalls, map layering/z‑index issues, and model compatibility quirks. This helped deliver a focused, production‑ready experience that PMs can trust.

T‑Insight was born from a simple question PMs ask daily: “Where are customers hurting right now, and what should we do about it?” Feedback is scattered across social media, outage trackers, forums, and support logs. We wanted a single pane of glass that turns raw noise into prioritized, location‑aware, actionable intelligence.

glance.what: AI platform to design buildings and simulate first-responder routes.
glance.why: Plans safer emergency response through optimized rescue routes.

record.what_it_is: A web-based emergency-response simulator: users build or import multi-floor building layouts, view them in 2D and 3D, place responders, victims and hazard zones, then run a turn-by-turn rescue simulation computed by a Python backend with route planning.
record.problem_and_user: Emergency planners, building designers and safety trainers wanting to test how layout and hazards affect rescue outcomes before real incidents.
record.one_line_pitch: Emergency-response simulator where users design multi-floor buildings in 2D/3D, place responders and victims, and run routed rescue simulations with hazards.
record.problem_statement: Planning how responders move and hazards spread in complex buildings is hard to test before a real disaster.
record.devpost_tagline: Search and Rescue is an AI-powered platform that lets users design buildings, create rescue scenarios, and simulate optimized first responder routes for safer emergency planning.
devpost_first_sections: Search and Rescue was inspired by the challenge of emergency response in complex buildings where every second matters. We wanted to create a system that could do more than just visualize a floor plan. Our goal was to build a platform that helps users think through how first responders move, how hazards spread, and how rescue outcomes change based on layout and decision-making. As engineering students, we were especially motivated by the idea of combining spatial design, simulation, and optimization into a tool that could have real-world safety applications.

Search and Rescue is an AI-powered emergency response simulation platform for planning and analysis. Users can design multi-floor buildings in 2D and 3D, define rescue scenarios, place responders and victims, and run simulations that model how emergency teams navigate a building. The system uses optimization and pathfinding techniques to assign responders and generate efficient routes while accounting for dynamic conditions such as fire or hostile threats. It is designed to help users evaluate layouts, improve preparedness, and better understand emergency response behavior before a real disaster happens.

glance.what: Cloud platform turning natural language into parallel high-performance pipelines.

record.what_it_is: A web-based HPC-native IDE where users describe a goal, an agentic Gemini-driven assistant builds a visual dataflow graph of a parallel workflow, and it runs locally or on AWS Batch with autoscaling workers.
record.problem_and_user: Researchers and newcomers blocked by the terminal-heavy complexity of HPC who want to run parallel workloads without schedulers or a CS background.
record.one_line_pitch: Web AI-native IDE for HPC that turns parallel workloads into a visual execution graph, with an agent that builds and debugs workflows and deploys to AWS Batch.
record.problem_statement: Using HPC requires terminal skills and scheduler knowledge that block researchers without a CS background.
record.devpost_tagline: Constellation is a HPC native IDE with seamless agentic AI integration that unlocks the world of HPC without needing another degree
devpost_first_sections: About Constellation Our inspiration was derived from the high barrier of entry to leveraging HPC for ones workload, particularly due to technical complexity. We set out to reduce this barrier. Constellation is based on the idea that parallel computing should be understood as data flow, with the technical complexity abstracted away. Constellation is an AI-native IDE designed specifically for HPC environments. It replaces terminal-heavy workflows that require a fundamental CS education with a visual execution graph and an agentic AI interface.

Constellation is implemented as a web-based IDE to maximize portability and ease of use. Users upload data and describe their goal in natural language, and Constellation assists the user in constructing, executing, and debugging parallel workflows, so they can focus on their research problems. Tasks are deployed in production clusters with AWS Batch, or ran locally on the backend for quick testing with smaller files. Scheduler scripts and batch logic are abstracted away, allowing users to focus on workload structure rather than job syntax. glance.what: Wrist guidance using voice, vision, and haptics to reach objects.
glance.why: Helps blind users reach objects safely and independently.

record.what_it_is: A soft fabric wristband with four vibration motors, one per cardinal direction, that tells blind or low-vision users which way to move their hand to reach an object. A spoken request and a phone camera feed a grounding backend that is meant to drive the motors via BLE.
record.problem_and_user: Blind and low-vision users who lack tools for small tasks such as finding and reaching an object on a table; inspired by a friend temporarily unable to see.
record.one_line_pitch: Fabric wristband with four haptic motors that cues blind and low-vision users which direction to move their hand to reach an object.
record.problem_statement: Assistive tools focus on navigation, with few helping blind users locate and reach small objects such as items on a table.
record.devpost_tagline: AI-powered wrist guidance that helps blind and low-vision people safely reach objects using voice, computer vision, and haptic feedback.
devpost_first_sections: Inspiration This project essentially started after one of our friends, after using steroid-based eye drops, had trouble seeing for 8 hours after using it. When we looked into assistive technology, we found so many of tools for navigation like smart walking canes, but fewer that focused on smaller tasks like finding an object on a table and reaching for it. We wanted to build something that could help with those everyday movements. Our V1 version at the start of the day used a large 3d printed bracelet with servo motors that physically pushed against the user’s hand to communicate direction. It gave us a starting point, but we wanted to make the device softer, less bulky, and easier to wear.

It is still a prototype. Then build better software that is actually scalable and has more use cases so it can help blind people in genuinely every way. Also potentially add more motors or wristbands on each hand so we can have more combinations of haptics to mean different things.

glance.what: Turns weather charts into broadcast-ready video reports with AI.
glance.why: Automates weather reporting for broadcasts and researchers.

record.what_it_is: A pipeline that takes a meteorological chart, has a vision LLM read it, writes a plain-language summary, voices it with TTS and lip-syncs an AI anchor to produce a TV-style weather video shown in a Streamlit dashboard.
record.problem_and_user: Meteorologists and researchers spend hours interpreting charts, and public weather communication is slow and manual; the public gets easier-to-consume forecasts.
record.one_line_pitch: Pipeline that turns weather charts into TV-style video reports using vision-LLM chart analysis, text summaries, synthetic narration and a lip-synced AI anchor.
record.problem_statement: Meteorologists spend hours manually interpreting charts and turning them into public communication.
record.devpost_tagline: Turn raw meteorological charts into broadcast-ready video reports with one click. Automate the weatherman and empower researchers.
devpost_first_sections: Meteorologists spend hours interpreting complex weather charts, yet public communication remains manual and time-consuming. We envisioned a world where AI could instantly translate raw atmospheric data into engaging video narratives ; democratizing access to weather insights while freeing experts to focus on research. Inspired by broadcast automation and climate tech innovation, NimbusNews bridges the gap between data and storytelling.

NimbusNews transforms weather charts (like 500 hPa vorticity maps) into TV-ready video reports : Analyzes charts using Llama 3.2 Vision AI to detect patterns (e.g., storm trajectories) Generates plain-language summaries with Llama 3.1 Converts text to lifelike audio via Deepgram AI Syncs narration to an AI anchor using modified open-source Wav2Lip Outputs, that are stored in AWS S3 can be viewed from the streamable dashboard.

glance.what: Sensor device that reminds rideshare riders of items left in cars.
glance.why: Stops people forgetting valuables in strangers' cars.

record.what_it_is: An in-car hardware and software system for rideshare: back-seat ultrasonic sensors detect riders leaving, a webcam photographs the cabin, a SambaNova-hosted vision LLM lists forgotten items, and the last rider gets a push notification with the photo.
record.problem_and_user: Rideshare riders who leave belongings in cars and drivers who spend time and fuel returning them.
record.one_line_pitch: In-car Raspberry Pi system detects when riders leave, photographs the back seat, has a vision LLM spot forgotten items, and notifies rider and driver.
record.problem_statement: Riders lose belongings in ride-share cars and drivers waste time and fuel returning them.
record.devpost_tagline: Backtracc reminds you of forgotten valuables when you leave rideshare vehicles because forgetting items in strangers' cars isn't fun.
devpost_first_sections: Search up ‘lost items’ on r/uber, and you’ll find countless stories people losing valuable possessions to Uber rides and other similar services. We all lose things at some point, but retrieving your stuff is usually a pain. Imagine this: you are very excited about your family vacation, and you decide to take an Uber to get to the airport. Once you get to the check-in gate, looking for your ID, you suddenly remember that you left your wallet in the Uber. Frantically, you try to get a hold of your driver, and the vacation is ruined as you wait for Uber to return your wallet - your flight has taken off without you and your family. You begrudgingly call another Uber to get you home. From the dri

Our project helps Uber drivers and riders by notifying both parties when items are left behind after their rides. Once a ride is completed, which we know when riders are no longer detected, we use a camera to check if there are any items left behind. If there are items left behind, our system will keep a log of it and will also send a notification instantly to the rider and driver as soon as possible.
